subject: Request: SLA variance for filter-induced tool-calling regressions
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@baytech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Marks <oliver.marks@baytech.com>, BayTech SRE <sre@baytech.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production impact: filtering causing tool-call failures and degraded structured outputs

Hi Irene —

Quick summary: since Friday we've observed a spike in content-filtering timeouts when our users invoke the invoice-parsing tool via your tool-calling API. The immediate user-visible effect is that structured JSON output fails to be produced ~4-7% of requests and instead returns a plain-text fallback. That fallback breaks our downstream automation (schema validation & downstream routing).

Attached is a short sample of error traces (baytech_error_samples.log) and three example payloads. We flagged these incidents under internal SUP-1234. This started after a model/infra push on Redwood's side (we believe around 2027-01-08).

Business impact: our reconciliation pipeline misses transactions; operations needs manual checks during peak hours. Estimated revenue at risk: low-mid six figures over the next quarter if not fixed.

Request:
- We need a formal SLA variance (temporary carve-out) for structured-output availability tied specifically to content-filtering/tool-calling interactions until a mitigation is deployed.
- Proposal: a 30-day variance window and an interim mitigation plan (graceful retry/backoff guidance + monitoring hooks).

Can you confirm next steps and what evidence you need from our side?

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Integrations, BayTech Payments

[attachment: baytech_error_samples.log (text/plain, 48KB)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@baytech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production impact: filtering causing tool-call failures and degraded structured outputs

Samira —

Really appreciate the clear write-up and logs. I'm escalating this to our reliability and product teams immediately. Quick responses:

- We see the traces you attached and they point to a filtering policy evaluation path that occasionally exceeds the tool-call timeout threshold.
- We're treating this as a high-priority SLO incident and will provide a mitigation plan by EOD tomorrow (11 Jan).

For the SLA variance request: we need to document the exact scope you want exempted (e.g., structured-output generation when a filter evaluation causes a tool-call to abort). If you can confirm the exact API routes/endpoints and example request IDs (you can paste a small set in the drive link) that would help speed our triage.

Interim ask from us: please upload request IDs and any sample tokens to the shared folder (we'll treat them as restricted evidence). We'll also generate a targeted instrumentation patch to capture timing percentiles in the filtering path.

I'll draft a temporary variance proposal and share it with you + legal tomorrow for review.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@baytech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production impact: filtering causing tool-call failures and degraded structured outputs

Hi all —

Triage notes from infra: we've reproduced the condition in our staging cluster. Root cause appears to be an interaction between a new regex-based moderation rule (deployed 2027-01-08) and the tool-calling preflight that forces additional synchronous checks. Under certain request shard loads the filter evaluation latency spikes to ~1.8s which exceeds the tool-call timeout of 1.5s. When that happens, the tool call is aborted and caller receives fallback text.

Planned mitigations:
- Short-term (48–72h): lower the new rule's priority for impacted routes and bump the tool-call timeout to 2.5s for BayTech's account as a scoped configuration. This is invasive but minimizes business impact quickly.
- Medium-term (2–4 weeks): introduce asynchronous filter evaluation with best-effort post-hoc enforcement for non-blocking tool-calls + a lightweight cache for recent predicate results.
- Monitoring: we'll push a dashboard for BayTech showing filter latency percentiles and fallback-rate per endpoint.

I'll open an internal change (SUP-1240) and attach a draft of the config change. Once Irene signs off we'll schedule the scoped timeout bump during a low-traffic window.

—Rishi
Sr. Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@baytech.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production impact: filtering causing tool-call failures and degraded structured outputs

Samira —

Thanks for raising this — value of quick coordination appreciated. From a customer/contract perspective, we can offer the following while the infra mitigations are implemented:

1) Temporary SLA variance window: 30 days from the date of configuration change. During this window we will not count structured-output fallbacks caused by verified filter-timeout conditions against BayTech's availability SLO for structured-output.

2) Economic remediation: if the fallback rate exceeds 3% in any rolling 7-day window during the variance period, we will apply a credit equal to 10% of that week’s invoice for affected endpoints, up to two billing cycles.

3) Mitigation deliverables: Rishi and team will provide a short runbook for graceful retries (client guidance) and a deployment timetable for the async filter evaluation.

We’ll need legal to sign off on the variance wording; I’ll loop them in once you confirm acceptance. Also please confirm the acceptance criteria for "verified filter-timeout conditions" (ideally request IDs + matching traces).

If BayTech is OK with the terms I can produce a short PDF (slo-variance-proposal-v1.pdf) and route for signatures.

—Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production impact: filtering causing tool-call failures and degraded structured outputs

Marissa / Irene —

Thanks — that sounds reasonable. We accept the 30-day variance window and the proposed economic remediation terms. We'll upload a set of verified request IDs and traces to the drive link by EOD today.

One ask: can the scoped timeout bump be applied to our production namespace during a Canary window next Monday (2027-01-18) morning? Our ops team will monitor and stand by.

Also: please include a clause that the variance applies only to errors where the filter evaluation is the proximate cause (not downstream tool logic). We'll provide the traces to support that.

—Samira

Subject: Re: Production impact: filtering causing tool-call failures and degraded structured outputs

Samira —

Thanks for the quick confirmation and for uploading the trace set. Summary / agreed plan below (finalized after legal review):

- Scope: Temporary SLA variance applies only to structured-output availability degradations directly attributable to verified content-filter evaluation latency (as determined by trace correlation and request IDs).
- Term: 30 days starting at the time we apply the scoped configuration change to your production namespace.
- Remediation economic terms: if fallback rate >3% in any rolling 7-day window, a 10% credit applies for that week, up to two billing cycles.
- Technical mitigations: Rishi will apply a scoped tool-call timeout bump to 2.5s in the Canary window on 2027-01-18 morning and monitor with BayTech. If stable, we'll roll to production and begin the asynchronous filter evaluation rollout (target 2–4 weeks).
- Evidence: BayTech to maintain request IDs and traces in the shared folder; we will use those traces to validate "verified filter-timeout conditions."

Next steps:
1) Rishi: schedule scoped timeout bump in Canary 2027-01-18 09:00-11:00 PT (confirm calendar invite).
2) Marissa: draft SLO variance PDF and route to legal for signatures (will attach slo-variance-proposal-v1.pdf).
3) BayTech: confirm monitoring standby and upload final evidence set.

I'll keep this thread updated with rollout progress. Appreciate the partnership and the detailed evidence — made the decision straightforward.

—Irene
Director, Customer Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
